question: Which of the following metals reacts with very dilute nitric acid to evolve hydrogen gas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manganese (Mn)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manganese (Mn)** reacts with very dilute nitric acid to evolve **hydrogen gas**.
 
• When dilute nitric acid is used, it acts as a typical acid releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• **Manganese** is a transition metal with the atomic number 25.
 
• Unlike other metals, when reacted with very dilute nitric acid, manganese releases **hydrogen gas** instead of producing nitrogen oxides.
 
• In most cases, nitric acid acts as a strong oxidizing agent, but in its dilute form, it can facilitate the release of hydrogen gas with certain metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aluminium (Al)**__

 __
 
• **Aluminium** reacts with nitric acid to form a passive oxide layer, preventing the release of hydrogen gas.
 
• This passive layer makes aluminium resistant to further reaction with nitric acid.
 
 
 
• **Iron (Fe)**__
 __
 
• **Iron** reacts with nitric acid, but instead of releasing hydrogen gas, it typically forms iron nitrate (Fe(NO₃)₃) and nitrogen oxides (NO or NO₂).
 
• Iron does not release hydrogen gas when reacted with nitric acid due to the oxidizing nature of nitric acid.
 
 
 
• **Zinc (Zn)**__
 
 
• **Zinc** reacts with nitric acid to form zinc nitrate (Zn(NO₃)₂) and nitrogen oxides (NO or NO₂), rather than releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• Like iron, the reaction of zinc with nitric acid results in the formation of nitrogen oxides due to the strong oxidizing properties of nitric acid.
